extension.description: Official repository for the Starfleet Kodi addon.

extension.summary: Starfleet - TV, Movies, Live TV, Sports, Radio, Adult
extension.description: All-in-one Kodi plugin. TV, Movies, Live TV, Sports, Free Streaming, Adult (PIN-protected), Radio. Torrent/debrid sources via Real-Debrid, AllDebrid, Premiumize, TorBox. Elementum support for magnet playback.
extension.news: v2.3.321 - Added optional TMDB List sync for the Favorite Movies/TV widgets (Settings â†’ Favorites â†’ TMDB List ID): enter the numeric ID from themoviedb.org/list/<id> and every device reads that one shared list instead of favoriting titles separately on each â€” TMDB lists can freely mix movies and TV. Confirmed live against a real 68-item public list that TMDB's list endpoint paginates at ~20/page even with no limit param set, so this fetches every page rather than silently truncating to the first 20. While a List ID is set, the long-press Add/Remove Favorites action shows a message pointing to themoviedb.org instead of writing to a local file that would have no visible effect. Leaving the setting blank keeps the existing per-device local Favorites behavior exactly as before. v2.3.320 - Fixed a real wrong-source bug found live via kodi.log: searching "Paradise S02E01" surfaced and pre-resolved AllDebrid streams for "Hell's Paradise" (Jigokuraku), a completely unrelated anime â€” the shared torrent title-match filter (used by every non-IMDB-based scraper: TPB, Knaben, 1337x, TGX, LimeTorrents, Bitsearch, TorLock, and others) only checked that the query phrase appeared as a contiguous substring anywhere in a torrent's title, so a longer, different show whose title merely ends with the same words passed as a false positive. Fixed by requiring the match to actually start the (release-tag-stripped) title, not sit after another real word. Torrentio (the one source that IS IMDB-tag-based) was already correct and unaffected. Also set Kodi's preferred audio language to English globally (once per session) â€” fixes multi-audio-track releases (e.g. a dubbed anime shipping both Japanese and English tracks) defaulting to whichever track happened to be first instead of English. Continuing the previous release's carousel-widget refresh fix. v2.3.319 - Fixed Home carousel widgets not refreshing after Favorites add/remove or Mark Watched/Unwatched from the long-press menu. Root cause: the long-press refresh only ever re-fetched the Live TV context's own Favorite Movies/TV rows â€” the Adult context's "Adult Favorites" row and the Radio context's "Continue Watching" row were never refetched, so a toggle there silently didn't show up until the next full background refresh. Both now refresh immediately too. Also removed Free Movies and Popcornflix from the Home carousel data-fetch â€” they were being scraped on every background refresh but never actually placed into any widget row (dead code), and per explicit request Movies/TV widgets should only ever pull from TMDB/TVDB, with Adult widgets staying Adult DVD Empire (ADE)-only, which they already were. v2.3.318 - Removed WeTrakr (the built-in scrobbler added in v2.3.315) for now, per request. Deleted wetrakr_auth.py and wetrakr_scrobble.py outright, removed the "Pair with WeTrakr" / status settings, and removed the scrobble-reporting hook from watch_history.py's playback monitor. Watch history, resume playback, and Trakt/SIMKL syncing are all unaffected â€” this only removes the separate WeTrakr scrobbling integration. v2.3.317 - Reverted Real-Debrid/AllDebrid/Premiumize/TorBox pairing back to native Settings â†’ Premium Services fields (enable toggle + API key entered directly here) â€” the ResolveURL-delegation approach from v2.3.312 ("pair everything in ResolveURL's own settings screen instead") turned out not to actually work for pairing in practice, per direct report that nothing happened when trying to pair. MegaDebrid and SimplyDebrid (added alongside that change) are kept as extra services per request, now also with their own native username/password fields here instead of ResolveURL's settings â€” no service requires opening ResolveURL's settings screen anymore. Existing enabled-service settings should carry over automatically since Kodi keeps stored setting values even while a schema temporarily stops exposing them; anyone who paired a service since v2.3.312 will need to re-enter its API key/credentials once here now that the fields are back. v2.3.316 - Fixed a real, long-standing bug: Continue Watching tracked and displayed watch progress correctly, but playback always started from 0:00 regardless â€” the saved resume position was never actually applied to seek the player. Confirmed via a full grep of the codebase that no play path anywhere set Kodi's ResumeTime/TotalTime, despite watch_history.py already storing exactly that data on every stop. Fixed by adding a shared apply_resume() helper and wiring it into every real play path: the main Movies/TV source picker (_unified_source_search, covering magnet/debrid, Elementum, and direct-stream plays alike), and â€” since the user specifically confirmed this needs to work from Home's own carousel/widget clicks too, not just the native menus â€” this same fix already covers those for free, since widget clicks route through the identical plugin:// play actions under the hood. Also extended to every Adult play path per a follow-up request ("adult resume also"): javseen/javleak/javhd, both ADE variants, HQ Porner, and the main AFDB search play. Along the way, found PandaMovies and the general AFDB-catalog stream-picker path had no watch-progress tracking at all (not even a watched checkmark) â€” added it so resume has something real to apply there too. Trailer picks are explicitly excluded everywhere, so a mostly-watched title's trailer never tries to seek past its own short runtime. Tested on desktop Kodi before this release. v2.3.315 - Added WeTrakr as a built-in, real-time scrobbler and a lightweight alternative to Trakt/SIMKL for watch-history tracking specifically (wetrakr.com) â€” new "Pair with WeTrakr" / "Check pairing status" buttons in Settings â†’ Premium Services, no Client ID needed at all (simpler than Trakt/SIMKL's own pairing). Reports "now playing" the moment playback starts, a progress update roughly once a minute, and a final position report when it stops â€” hooked into the same playback monitor every movie/TV/adult play path already calls through, so it's active everywhere automatically with zero extra wiring, and a genuine no-op (no thread, no network call) whenever no account is paired. Also fixed sports event times not showing device-local time for this session's two newest sources: confirmed the existing time-conversion logic was already correct, the real gap was that mut.st and sportsbite.org's own scrapers never captured a timestamp at all â€” sportsbite.org already provides one directly (trivial fix), mut.st only gives a string like "05:30 PM PST - (07/30/2026)" so a proper timezone-aware parser was added (using Python's zoneinfo, so daylight saving is handled correctly instead of a static offset table that would silently drift wrong half the year). Only affects data from each source's next scheduled scrape, not what's already live. Also looked into a dedicated "resolveurlxxx" adult-hoster resolver module per request â€” every variant checked (jsergio123's, Dogg006's, qwarlock's) has sat untouched for 2+ years, while the ResolveURL fork this addon already depends on was pushed 5 days ago â€” not worth adding a stale dependency when this session already built substantial native Adult scraping infrastructure covering the same need. v2.3.314 - Four changes, tested on desktop before this release: (1) Fixed a real navigation bug where drilling into any nested screen (confirmed with Adult â†’ Movies â†’ New Releases) and backing all the way out would snap Home back to the Movies carousel at its last remembered position instead of staying on whatever section you were actually in â€” root cause was Starfleet-Home.xml's defaultcontrol="always", which force-refocuses the hero Play button every time Home reactivates (not just on first load), and the skin's own static nav wiring off that button routes toward Movies. Fixed by only applying it on first load. (2) The carousel's long-press Favorites/Watched menu now calls the underlying functions directly and synchronously instead of firing an async background action, then immediately re-renders the carousel â€” so a toggle shows up right away instead of only after the next full Home reopen. (3) Every TMDB-backed carousel row (New Releases, Popular, Top Rated, Trending, TV Popular/Top Rated/Airing/On The Air, Free Movies, Popcornflix, Adult New Releases/Recently Added, Trakt Anticipated) now fetches ~4 pages instead of 1 â€” roughly 60-100 items per row instead of ~20 â€” also fixed the Trakt widgets, whose own limit= parameter turned out to be silently ignored since they only ever fetched one page regardless of what was passed in. (4) Dropped toutv (Radio-Canada's TOU.TV) from the shared scraper task list â€” confirmed live returning 0 results across dozens of real Adult searches in a row (a mainstream French-Canadian public broadcaster's catalog was never a realistic source for that content), and since it ran unconditionally on every Movies/TV/Adult search alike, removing it trims one more always-run source out of every single search's wait, not just Adult's. v2.3.313 - Removed Google Drive cross-device sync entirely, per explicit request that it doesn't work. Deleted gdrive_auth.py and gdrive_sync.py outright, removed the whole "Google Drive" settings section (Client ID/Secret, Link/Status/Sync-now/auto-sync toggle, internal token fields), removed the sync-trigger calls in Home's open/close and Back-handling paths, and removed the now-unused export_db()/import_db() helpers from watch_history.py, favorites.py, and adult_favorites.py that existed solely to feed this feature. Watch history, favorites, and adult favorites are all still fully local â€” this addon has no cross-device sync mechanism of any kind now. v2.3.312 - Migrated Real-Debrid, AllDebrid, Premiumize, and TorBox pairing to ResolveURL (already a hard dependency of this addon), and added MegaDebrid and SimplyDebrid as two brand-new premium services the same way â€” the same architecture "the crew" uses for all six of these. Pairing now happens entirely in ResolveURL's own settings screen (a new "Open ResolveURL Settings" button in Settings â†’ Premium Services takes you straight there) â€” Real-Debrid/AllDebrid/Premiumize/TorBox use ResolveURL's own PIN or OAuth dialogs, MegaDebrid/SimplyDebrid use a plain username+password field there. This addon no longer stores any of these six services' credentials itself; it reads whichever ones are already paired in ResolveURL and still makes the actual resolve calls natively (kept native rather than delegated, for full control over logging/error handling â€” this addon's own real streaming features don't change). Verified by reading ResolveURL's actual installed settings and confirming its real setting-ID naming (e.g. AllDebridResolver_token) matches exactly what the new code reads. Magnet/torrent resolution (a separate mechanism from simple link-unrestrict) is untouched for Real-Debrid/AllDebrid/Premiumize/TorBox â€” MegaDebrid/SimplyDebrid have no torrent-caching backend of their own so they only ever apply to plain scraped hoster links, same limitation as on their native sites. v2.3.311 - Added two new sports sources per user request (investigated 12 candidate sites total, honest results below). Both real, verified end-to-end before shipping via the same JSON-orchestrator pipeline every other sports source already uses (streameast/crackstreams/all24/daddylive): mut.st (MutStreams) resolved 79 real events across 11 categories (NFL, NBA, soccer, MLB, motorsports, wrestling, cricket, rugby, darts, tennis, and a general "other" bucket); sportsbite.org resolved 2 real MLB events via a separate backend (api.watchfooty.st) discovered by watching its own network traffic, not guessed. Honest results on the rest: ppv.st/.cx/.is/.lc (all four are one shared backend/frontend) have real event data but every stream embed routes through embedindia.st, which runs a WASM-based anti-bot challenge headless Chromium never gets past â€” confirmed live, zero stream requests ever fire, not shippable. streamed.pk/.st's own events API works but its stream-resolve endpoint returns empty for every match tried. strmfree.st/streamfree.top's real player page is gated behind an ad-injection overlay that intercepts the click needed to start playback. bintv.cc (Blogger-hosted) and ondemand.st need more reverse-engineering than this round covered â€” no scraper built for either yet. v2.3.310 - Added long-press on the Home screen's own carousel rows (Movies, TV Shows, Trakt Anticipated, Live's favorited rows, and Continue Watching) â€” Add/Remove Favorites and Mark as Watched/Unwatched, the same two actions every full category screen's long-press menu already had, now reachable directly from the home carousel without drilling into a category first. Adult carousel rows use the same Adult Favorites/wh_key-based watched toggle every other Adult long-press menu in the addon already uses. Rows with nothing meaningful to favorite (today's live sports games, which carry no stable id) simply show no menu on long-press rather than a broken one. v2.3.309 - Added Internet Archive (archive.org) as a real free streaming source, built from scratch â€” the addon's own code already had dead, unused plumbing expecting an "archive_id" field and a resolve_archive_stream() function that never existed anywhere; both are now real. Movies search archive.org's 28,000+ item feature_films collection; TV searches classic_tv specifically (confirmed live â€” the much bigger generic "television" collection is overwhelmingly random local news broadcasts, not real named shows, so it's deliberately not used). Every match is resolved to its real playable video file, filtering out the thumbnail/torrent/metadata sidecar files archive.org bundles alongside the actual video on every item. Wired in two ways: (1) participates automatically in the normal Movies/TV "choose a source" search used everywhere else in the addon, and (2) added as a real, browsable "Internet Archive" entry in the Free Movies and Free TV Shows service lists (this second path already had a dead, unreachable branch in the code expecting it â€” now finished and reachable). Verified live end-to-end before shipping: real search+resolve for a movie, real search+resolve for a TV episode, and real paginated browse listings for both. Honest limitation: TV episode search matches by exact title text, and archive.org's own item titles don't follow a "Show S01E01" naming convention, so expect real hits there to be rarer than for movies â€” same disclosed tradeoff already made for MyPornClub search in an earlier release. v2.3.308 - Fixed Adult Search â€” the one remaining Adult screen that still dropped out of the addon's own three-panel skin into a plain native Kodi listing (styled by whatever system skin is active, not ours) instead of staying in-process like every other Adult category already does. Extracted the real search logic (category/tag match, performer match, ADE+AFDB title search, plus XXXClub/Rintor torrent and free-stream results) out of the native page into a shared function so both the old native listing and the new in-process version use the exact same search â€” nothing about what a search actually finds has changed, only where results are shown. Raw torrent/stream hits (which are already one specific playable link, not a browsable film) get their own "Info" and direct-play handling rather than being forced through the normal multi-source picker a second time. Also answered a question honestly rather than just saying yes: audited exactly what's pulled from TMDB/TVDB right now versus what both APIs actually offer â€” real gaps exist (content ratings, full crew beyond director/writers, TVDB's own show-level data and artwork, next-episode-to-air/in-production status, per-episode guest stars, network/studio logos) â€” nothing shipped this release, flagged for a future pass if wanted. v2.3.307 - Replaced the dead TheTVDB API key with a fresh one you generated, verified live before wiring it in (real login, real token). This turns out to be a real upgrade for TV episode data, not just a restoration: tested against the same show as last release, TVDB has real per-episode overviews and even future episodes' titles and air dates already listed days/weeks ahead, which neither TMDB nor the episodate.com backstop added last release could offer â€” TVDB now goes first in the season-fetch cross-check, with episodate.com staying as a second-tier backstop for whatever TVDB itself doesn't have. Also fixed a real, separate bug this surfaced: TVDB's own episode image field is already a full URL, but the code was prepending the base URL again on top of it, producing a broken doubled-domain link that could never load â€” never caught before now since the dead key meant this code path never actually ran. All of this funnels through the one shared season-fetching function every episode list already reads from, so it reaches TV episode browsing, Continue Watching, and auto-play-next alike, same as last release's fix. v2.3.306 - Fixed episodes missing from a season's listing when TMDB simply hasn't caught up yet â€” reported live and verified against the real show (TMDB's own API for "Maine Cabin Masters: All-Inn" season 1 genuinely only listed episode 1 days after episode 2 had already aired). Checked the obvious alternatives first: IMDb's own site is behind an AWS WAF JS challenge and can't be scraped without a full headless browser (confirmed live, not assumed); this addon's existing TheTVDB integration would have been the natural fix, but its API key is dead (confirmed via a real login attempt â€” "InvalidAPIKey"), and a spare copy of the same key found in an old backup archive turned out to be the identical dead key, not a working replacement. Landed on episodate.com instead â€” a free service needing no API key at all, built on TVDB's own dataset â€” which already had episode 2 with the right air date when TMDB didn't. Wired into the one shared season-fetching function every episode list in the addon already goes through (TV episode browsing, Continue Watching's next-episode detection, and auto-play-next all funnel through get_season_detail), so this one fix reaches everywhere episodes are read from, not just one screen. TMDB's own entry always wins when both sources list the same episode â€” this only fills in episode numbers TMDB is missing outright, never overrides or duplicates what TMDB already has. v2.3.305 - Fixed Continue Watching's "next episode" cards showing the episode's own still image instead of the series poster â€” every other row in this addon shows the series icon, this one alone was showing a random episode frame instead. Added a real "Info" long-press option to every real Movies/TV Shows/Adult browsing screen (New Releases/Popular/Top Rated/Upcoming, genre lists, Favourites, Search, and Adult's New Releases/Recently Added/Best Sellers/Full Library/HQ Porner) â€” selecting it opens the exact same rich full-metadata screen (poster, cast with photos, plot, director/genres/studio, Play/Trailer/Favorite) the home carousel's Upcoming widget already uses, reused as-is rather than building a second screen: for Adult it now also supports favoriting through the separate adult_favorites store and correctly source-routes its detail fetch (ADE vs AFDB vs free-stream, since Full Library mixes all three with incompatible id/slug namespaces â€” same routing fix shipped for the side-panel a few releases back, applied here too). Deliberately left out for this round: genre/category picker screens (their tiles aren't real titles), Channels lists, and Live TV/Sports/Radio/JAV, which weren't part of what was asked for. v2.3.304 - Changed magnet/Elementum policy per explicit instruction: previously every magnet play path tried debrid first but still fell back to Elementum for that one torrent specifically if debrid couldn't resolve it within its poll window â€” even with a debrid service enabled. Elementum is now ONLY ever used when NO debrid service is enabled at all; with any debrid service on, a magnet debrid can't resolve now fails cleanly with a "Debrid could not resolve this torrent" notice instead of quietly falling through to Elementum. Applied consistently across all four places a magnet could reach Elementum: Adult's ADE-sourced play path (afdb_router.adult_stream_play, covers Full Library and every other Adult category), the native XXXClub browse-and-play action, Movies/TV's unified source search, and the Free-Streaming router â€” the last of these hadn't even tried debrid for a magnet at all before this, going straight to Elementum unconditionally regardless of what was enabled. Investigated the "Full Library still goes to Elementum" report by live-testing the real AllDebrid API directly with a real account: confirmed the actual polling/parsing code is correct against AllDebrid's current v4.1 API (verified a real magnet/status response resolves correctly end to end) â€” the behavior being reported was the previous intentional-but-unwanted design (debrid tried, then Elementum as fallback per-torrent), not a parsing bug, which is what this release actually changes. v2.3.303 - Fixed MyPornClub returning zero results in every actual Adult search (confirmed live against the real site, not guessed): its search-result pages (/s/<query>) link each post with an extra "?sk=...&sp=...&ss=..." suffix after the post id that the browse page's own plain links don't have, and the id-matching regex expected the closing quote right after the id â€” so it matched the browse page fine (that's what got tested before) but matched zero posts on every real search, silently, every time. Fixed to tolerate the suffix. Fixed Full Library's metadata (plot/cast) not loading for a real chunk of its titles: Full Library merges three different sources with incompatible id/slug namespaces (adultdvdempire.com, a completely separate "AFDB" site at adultfilmdatabase.com, and free-stream stubs) but always queried the first site regardless of which one a title actually came from â€” an AFDB id looked up against the wrong site just returns nothing. Now routed to the correct source per item. Fixed Full Library's pagination being real but practically undiscoverable: "Next Page" existed already (added last release) but was buried as a menu option inside the same "More Sections" picker used for jumping to New Releases/Recently Added/etc, under a button that still said "More Sections" either way â€” the button itself now says "Next Page (X/Y)" and goes straight there when there's one, instead of opening a picker to find it. Also confirmed live: ext.to's Cloudflare protection has gotten stronger since it was added two releases ago â€” even cloudscraper's bypass now gets served the JS challenge page instead of real results, so it's effectively non-functional right now until that's solved properly; flagging honestly rather than leaving it silently broken. v2.3.302 - Fixed automatic "mark as watched" and TV auto-play-next both silently never firing â€” root-caused via direct code reading, one single bug behind both: the playback monitor read the final position (getTotalTime/getTime) only AFTER Kodi's player had already stopped, but Kodi's Player API throws once playback is no longer active ("no active file"), which was being swallowed into "0 watched seconds" every single time regardless of how far you actually got through something. Since both the automatic watched-write and the auto-play-next decision depend on that position being real, this made the manual "Mark as Watched" toggle (which never touches the Player object at all) the only path that ever actually worked â€” exactly matching what was reported. Now the position is captured on every poll WHILE still playing, so the last real value survives instead of always reading back zero right after the fact. Applies to movies and TV episodes both, since they share the same monitor. v2.3.301 - Added Google Drive as a cross-device sync option for watch history, favorites, and adult favorites (Settings > Sync) â€” separate from Trakt/SIMKL above, and not a watch-tracking service: this creates one small JSON file in your own Google Drive (scoped so the addon can only ever see that one file it created, nothing else in your Drive) and merges it with whatever's on each device signed into the same Google account. Merging is last-write-wins per item using the timestamp every entry already carried before this existed, so a favorite added on one device and a show marked watched on another in the same window both survive â€” only a genuine same-item conflict picks whichever side is more recent. Syncs automatically when Home opens (pulls) and closes (pushes), both fire-and-forget so a slow or unreachable network never delays anything visible, plus a manual "Sync now" action. Needs a free Google OAuth client same as Trakt/SIMKL's BYO-key setup. Verified the actual merge logic against fabricated data before shipping; the live Google OAuth device-flow and real Drive API calls could not be tested end-to-end here (no paired Google account available in this environment) â€” the code follows Drive API v3's documented request format exactly, but this one genuinely needs a real test pass on your end before trusting it with a second device. v2.3.300 - Re-confirmed ext.to is wired into the unified search exactly the same way as Knaben (one unconditional entry, same tasks dict, same call shape) â€” no change needed there, already live in v2.3.297+. The Radio nav button's carousel (which had no real content of its own â€” it was just quietly reusing the same rows as the Movies tab) now shows Continue Watching instead. This isn't just "resume the one thing you stopped mid-episode": a TV show stays in Continue Watching as long as ANY unwatched episode exists anywhere in its real catalog â€” finishing all of Season 1 still surfaces the show if Season 2 exists and hasn't been touched at all, using the show's actual TMDB episode list rather than only what's already in local watch history. If the very next unwatched slot is a season that hasn't released yet (announced but no air date, or a real future date), the card shows its release date instead of trying to play something that isn't out. Movies still show as plain in-progress resume cards. One real limitation, disclosed honestly rather than silently: this needs a tmdb_id recorded per watch-history entry to look up the show's episode catalog at all â€” episodes played before this release didn't store one, so a show only reappears in Continue Watching once at least one more episode of it gets played (going forward, every play now records it). Verified the core grouping/next-episode/upcoming-season logic against fabricated watch-history data before shipping (no live Kodi session available here to click through it) â€” worth a real test pass on your end. v2.3.299 - Actually found the real cause of the Adult Full Library navigation bug this time, after two earlier releases fixed real-but-insufficient bugs in the same area: your own log confirmed Full Library currently merges 9,576 titles, and the custom category list was loading ALL of them into the on-screen list in a single synchronous pass every time the screen opened â€” building ~9,500 ListItems back-to-back on the GUI thread is enough on its own to back up Kodi's input queue for seconds regardless of anything else running in the background, which is exactly what read as broken Up/Down/Back. This wasn't a code regression â€” the same list-building code has been structurally unchanged for a dozen releases â€” it's that the merged catalog itself has grown large enough to cross into "visibly blocks the GUI" territory, which also explains why this used to work fine. Fixed by actually paginating Full Library locally (300 titles per page, via the existing "More Sections" button, which now offers "Next Page" first when there's one) instead of ever handing the whole catalog to the list at once; New Releases/Recently Added/Best Sellers are far smaller and render exactly as before, unpaged. Also confirmed: the checkmark for "watched" is a real image overlay (checkmark.png), not just text, already wired correctly in the skin and gated on the same property the last release's toggle-crash fix now sets correctly â€” and ext.to is wired into the unified torrent search (search_all) exactly the same way as TPB/Knaben/every other generic source: one unconditional entry in the same tasks dict, no special-casing, so it runs for Movies/TV/Adult right alongside them. v2.3.298 - Found via your own fresh log from testing v2.3.297, not guesswork: (1) the "Mark as Watched/Unwatched" context-menu toggle for Movies and TV shows was crashing outright (AttributeError in dispatcher.py â€” a helper's string default got called with an int default instead, which blew up trying to unquote it) whenever season/episode weren't in the URL, i.e. every single Movie/TV-show toggle; fixed, and added the same manual watched-toggle to Adult's browsing categories (New Releases/Recently Added/Best Sellers/Full Library), which never had one â€” Adult still gets the checkmark automatically from real playback either way. (2) A real thread race in the shared SQLite cache's one-time init (many modules each call it independently at import time, and Kodi's first navigation imports several concurrently) could let two threads open the connection and issue startup PRAGMAs simultaneously â€” confirmed live as the exact "Safety level may not be changed inside a transaction" crash out of the Movies menu in the same log; now guarded with a proper lock. (3) Real-Debrid/AllDebrid's ~60-second cache-poll (added last release specifically to stop good torrents falling back to Elementum early) was being silently cut off after just 20-25 seconds by an internal aggregation timeout and by every caller's own timeout on top of that â€” across Movies, TV, and all three Adult play paths â€” meaning it almost never got the full window it was built for; every one of those timeouts now actually covers the poll's real duration, so torrents that aren't instantly cached get a genuine shot at RD/AD before Elementum is used at all. Also: MyPornClub is now wired as a parallel search source (same role as XXXClub/ext.to) in a third Adult play path that had XXXClub but not it. As with the nav/Back fix last release, these are reasoned from direct code + log reading, not confirmed against a fresh live session â€” worth a real test pass. v2.3.297 - Added ext.to as a new torrent/magnet source (Movies, TV, and Adult) â€” rewired to its real, current site structure (/browse/?q=...&cat=N with a plain HTML table, not the stale search endpoint the old scraper targeted), and wired directly into both Adult play paths alongside XXXClub/Rintor/MyPornClub. Removed MyPornClub as its own standalone browsable menu section â€” it's now only a parallel search source feeding the Adult stream picker, same role as XXXClub/Rintor, per request. Root-caused (via direct code reading, not guesswork) the recurring Adult Full Library navigation bug and the new "Back doesn't exit the category" regression: the category list's onInit() was eagerly computing a full context menu for every single item during population, including a real uncached disk read for Adult's favorite-status check â€” for a large list like Full Library this could block the GUI thread for seconds, during which Kodi queues and misapplies Up/Down/Back presses, which is what read as the highlight jumping back and Back not responding. That eager computation was confirmed dead code (this window's context menu is actually shown a different way, on long-press, computed fresh for one item at a time) so it's removed outright, plus a defensive guard so a background detail-fetch thread can no longer touch a control after the window's already been closed via Back. This is reasoned from the code, not confirmed against a live Kodi session in this environment â€” flagging that honestly rather than claiming it's verified fixed. v2.3.296 - Real-Debrid and AllDebrid now get a genuine, full attempt on every magnet before ever falling back to Elementum, not just an instant cache check. AllDebrid in particular only ever checked its upload response's "ready" flag once, immediately, and gave up right away if that torrent wasn't already sitting in cache â€” even a well-seeded torrent it could fetch quickly never got any time to become ready at all. Both RD and AD now poll for up to ~60 seconds (a themed, cancellable progress dialog shows while this happens, so it never just looks like Kodi hung) before giving up and falling through to Elementum. Premiumize/TorBox untouched â€” their own cache-check endpoints are already reliable, unlike RD/AD's, so there's no meaningful wait to extend there. v2.3.295 - Fixed a real navigation bug in the custom-skin category lists (Adult Full Library, but affects any category with a detail_fetch â€” Movies/TV/Sports/Adult): the per-focus detail fetch (a real network call for cast/plot/venue photo) was running INLINE on the same thread that handles Up/Down key presses, blocking it for the fetch's whole duration. Pressing Down again before it returned queued up input that all landed at once the instant it finally did, on a now-stale position â€” reading as the highlight randomly jumping back to an earlier row. A staleness guard for exactly this race already existed in the code but never had anything to actually race against, since nothing ran in the background before. Fixed by actually running the fetch on a background thread. (Investigated a report of a debrid-cached magnet routing to Elementum instead of AllDebrid: debrid resolution only ever resolves a torrent that's already instantly cached on that service â€” if that specific one wasn't, falling back to Elementum is the correct, existing behavior, not a bug. Couldn't confirm either way from the log provided since it didn't cover that playback attempt at all.) v2.3.294 - Added myporn.club as a new Adult source: confirmed live (via direct scraping, not guesswork) that its own "search" is really just a single-tag browse page â€” a real multi-word title search 404s outright, and even a distinctive word like a performer's name returns nothing since it isn't one of the site's own hashtags â€” so rather than force it into the same per-title search role XXXClub has (where it would rarely find anything), it's wired in two ways: as a genuine extra parallel search source in the existing Adult picker (same role as XXXClub, lower hit rate given the above), and as its own new browsable "MyPornClub" section under the Adult menu (a latest-uploads feed, working end-to-end off the site's real embedded stream links). Also: TV episodes now show cast with photos in the metadata panel, same as Movies/Adult (the show's own cast) â€” previously that space was reserved entirely for the episode still image. And: attempted a second fix for the "Choose source" picker's Cancel button using the same list->scrollbar->button escape route Kodi's own native select dialog uses internally (skin.estuary) â€” the list's own in-row Cancel entry from last release remains the guaranteed-working way to reach it regardless. v2.3.293 - Added a new TV Shows setting: "Automatically play the next episode" (off by default), with a configurable cancellable countdown before it kicks in. When an episode finishes (genuinely finishes â€” a manual early stop never triggers it), Starfleet looks up the next episode (rolling into the next season automatically once one runs out) and plays it the same way as picking it manually, sources and all. Also fixed two spots in the movie/TV playback path that were silently missing the tmdb_id needed for the watched-status bridge added last release (only one of three call sites had actually gotten it). v2.3.292 - Fixed the watched/in-progress checkmark never actually showing up, root-caused via a direct reproduction (not guesswork): watch_history.py cached its data in memory after the first read and never refreshed it â€” harmless for a normal Kodi plugin (each menu action is its own short-lived process), but this addon's Home/Movies/TV/Adult screens stay open as one long-lived process for the whole session, so once that first read happened, it kept serving the same stale (pre-watched) snapshot for the rest of the session no matter how many times a separate "Mark as Watched" action or a finished movie/episode correctly wrote the real update to disk â€” confirmed exactly this with a standalone reproduction before and after the fix. Also: the TV episode list never had a working long-press "Mark as Watched/Unwatched" option at all (confirmed live long-press already worked fine for movies) â€” it's wired in now, using the same show identifier the episode list itself already reads watched status from, so a manual toggle always lands under the exact key that gets checked. v2.3.291 - Actually fixed the themed "Choose source" picker's Cancel navigation this time â€” confirmed live (via direct testing) that the previous release's code-level fix still didn't work, because the real root cause was different than diagnosed: the list control itself was swallowing the Up/Right key press at the boundary before the window's own code ever saw it, a genuine Kodi limitation for this dialog type, not something fixable by intercepting the key press in Python. Rather than keep fighting that, Cancel is now a real row inside the list itself (last item, in orange) â€” reachable the exact same proven way every other row already is: scroll to it and press OK. The original Cancel button in the corner is left in place for mouse/touch clicks, but the list row is the real d-pad path now. v2.3.290 - Fixed the themed "Choose source" picker's Cancel button still being unreachable via Up on the d-pad after last release's XML nav fix â€” that fix relied on the list control's own <onup> declaration, which is confirmed live to not reliably fire at the list's top boundary in this bespoke dialog window. Now handled explicitly in code instead: pressing Up while the top row is focused forces focus onto Cancel directly, the same "don't rely on native bespoke-window behavior, do it ourselves" fix already used for this dialog's own long-press context menu. v2.3.289 - Added a watched/unwatched/in-progress indicator across Movies, TV, and Adult browsing: a checkmark shows on anything already finished, a percentage on anything partway through, backed by the same watch_history.json store this addon already kept in the Kodi profile folder (outside the addon's own code directory, so it already survived updates before this â€” no separate persistence work needed, just making it visible). Movies/TV list screens only ever carry a tmdb_id (TMDB's list endpoints don't expose imdb_id, and fetching it per item would mean an extra API call for every title on screen), so a new bridge key is written alongside the existing imdb_id-keyed entry at play time and by the manual Mark as Watched/Unwatched toggle, letting these lists check watched status with no extra network calls. Also added a dedicated release-year line (movies) / air-date line (TV episodes) to the three-panel metadata pages, instead of no date info being shown there at all. Fixed the themed "Choose source" picker dialog: pressing Up from the option list looped back on itself instead of reaching the Cancel button sitting visually above it. v2.3.288 - Removed the NowTV embed source (myfilestorage.xyz) â€” confirmed live it's been permanently dead since it stopped resolving anything: the domain itself has expired and is now sitting parked/for-sale, returning an HTTP 200 "this domain may be for sale" placeholder page for every request, real title or not, since there's no file host behind it anymore. Our own success check only looked at the status code, so it always looked like a real hit and always failed to actually play â€” removed rather than left as a permanently-broken option in the source picker. v2.3.287 - Restored Radio to the main navigation â€” it had been fully working on the backend this whole time (country/state/city/station browsing, search, playback) but got orphaned from the UI once the custom Home skin replaced the native menu that used to list it, so there was no way to actually reach it anymore. Added a Radio button to the nav bar and built the same three-panel browsing flow (with the themed dialogs) the rest of the addon already has: countries -> states/provinces -> cities -> stations, quick-access country shortcuts, and search â€” all backed by the exact same resolution and playback logic as before, just with a way to get to it again. v2.3.286 - Themed three more native Kodi dialogs to match the rest of the addon (navy/orange, Starfleet icon) instead of whatever the user's active system skin looks like: the "Choose source"/stream picker (previously the native blue-highlight select list), and the busy spinner shown while browsing Adult movies (previously Kodi's default spinner). Both are real WindowXMLDialog replacements built the same way the progress dialog was last release, since native dialogs are rendered by the active system skin and can't be branded through the addon's own bundled skin folder otherwise. v2.3.285 - Fixed AllDebrid, Real-Debrid, Premiumize, and TorBox magnet resolution: AllDebrid and Real-Debrid's own bulk cache-check endpoints are both confirmed dead/unreliable now, which meant enabling either service still silently fell through to Elementum regardless of whether a torrent was actually cached - fixed by relying on each service's real add/upload attempt as the cache check instead (verified live end-to-end against AllDebrid with a real account and a real magnet). The second-chance magnet resolver used by Movies/TV/Adult playback only supported Real-Debrid and AllDebrid before - a Premiumize- or TorBox-only setup would skip straight to Elementum even with debrid enabled; now all four services are tried, in the priority order set in Settings. Confirmed the full chain is correct end to end: every enabled debrid service is tried before Elementum for movies, TV, and Adult magnets, and Elementum runs immediately with no added delay when no debrid service is enabled. Sports: added the missing Soccer icon (was still using a generic remote icon) and confirmed the full custom icon set is present. Movies/TV: added custom icons for the Action, Adventure, Animation, Comedy, Crime, and Documentary genre lists (other genres unchanged). v2.3.225 - Sports: fixed several menu/listing issues confirmed live tonight. TotalSportek24 (tstek) events always showed no LIVE tag regardless of actual status - was hardcoded false; now derived from whether the event's start time has recently passed (combat-sports cards run long, so a 5h window is used). UFC/Boxing/WWE/Tennis events with no parseable date from TheSportsDB now show "TBD" instead of a blank time, and one malformed record from that API can no longer blank out the rest of that day's events. NHL Network: onhockey.tv's own pages now gate the real player behind a nested same-domain iframe a single-page scrape can't follow (confirmed live - neither the dedicated page nor the old daddylive-wrapper page expose an extractable stream anymore) - switched to the same daddylive.mov channel-id resolver already used elsewhere. MLB Network: root-caused a real 403/no-stream failure to one mirror host (cdnlivetv.tv) using a new obfuscation scheme - the stream URL is split into ~10 separately base64-encoded fragments assembled by an in-page JS function, not the single XOR blob this resolver already handled - added a decoder for it and verified live it now returns a real, playable #EXTM3U playlist. Also fixed a filter bug in the debrid torrent-search path that could silently drop a legitimate movie/TV torrent if its uploader's display name happened to contain ".com" (e.g. an embedded site tag) - that string was incorrectly treated the same as a real non-video file extension (.exe/.zip/etc). Removed a leftover duplicate, unused search_torrentio() definition. (Investigated a report of Elementum/magnet playback being broken by this update - confirmed both the magnet-search and Elementum hand-off code are unchanged and correct; the specific case reported was simply an episode that hadn't been released yet, so no torrents existed anywhere for it yet.) v2.3.224 - Added a "Clear cache" button (Settings, top of the debrid/resolver section) - explains a real discrepancy found live tonight (Windows showed the new CFL menu entry, the same device's Firestick didn't): the Sports category list is cached 24h, and updating the addon's code doesn't invalidate an already-cached result from before the update - a device that browsed Sports earlier keeps serving the old list for the rest of that window regardless of version. Android also blocks ADB/file-manager access to the addon's own private data directory, so there was no way to force this without the app itself doing it - this button does it from inside Kodi's own Settings UI, no ADB or file access needed. v2.3.223 - Fixed a regression from v2.3.220's Adult title-cleaning: the bare word "XXX" was being stripped out of every title anywhere it appeared, but that word is frequently a real, intentional part of adult film titles (e.g. "The Odyssey: A XXX Parody" - a parody title genre convention), not junk. Stripping it mangled the title before it was used to cross-reference the real catalog for high-quality cover art, so that lookup stopped matching and posters fell back to nothing - confirmed live. Now only strips "XXX" when it's clearly its own bracketed tag, e.g. "(XXX)" or "[XXX]" with nothing else inside, which doesn't collide with a title that legitimately contains the word. v2.3.222 - Fixed Adult section listings collapsing to almost nothing after a few hours of real use (confirmed live: New Releases went from showing real content to showing none at all). Root cause was in the has-a-source filter added in v2.3.220: it decided whether to hide a title based on a passive index of whatever detail pages happened to already be cached from past browsing - early on that index is empty (lenient, shows everything), but after enough browsing it becomes non-empty while still being nowhere near a complete picture, and the filter started treating "never actually checked" the same as "confirmed no source", hiding almost everything. Fixed at the source: added a real, separate "confirmed no source" record that's only written after an actual search for that exact title comes back empty, and the filter now only hides a title once that's genuinely happened - titles it hasn't gotten to yet keep showing immediately like before, and only get hidden once really confirmed absent, so the list starts accurate and gets more accurate over time instead of collapsing. Also found (separate issue, not yet fixed): Adult DVD Empire's movie trailers are dead through this addon's existing trailer URL formula - checked a real, current film page directly and that entire domain/path pattern doesn't exist anymore; the site has moved trailers to a different domain requiring a per-scene ID this addon doesn't currently track, not just a movie ID. Needs its own scraper work to properly fix - flagged for a follow-up rather than a rushed fix tonight. v2.3.221 - EMERGENCY FIX: v2.3.220's bytecode-only build completely broke the addon - confirmed live via kodi.log that every single plugin:// call failed with "ImportError: bad magic number in 'resources'". The bytecode was correctly compiled for Python 3.11.9 (verified before shipping), but Kodi's own bundled Python 3.11 build on this device uses a different internal magic number stamp than standalone Python 3.11.9 - the exact version-mismatch risk flagged before attempting this, just at a finer-grained level (same Kodi major version, different bundled interpreter patch) than expected. Reverted immediately to plain, uncompiled source - identical code to v2.3.220, just not bytecode-compiled - to restore a working addon. No further obfuscation attempts until a build approach can be verified against Kodi's actual bundled interpreter directly rather than a same-numbered standalone Python install. v2.3.220 - Fixed CFL (and College Football/CFB) missing from the Sports menu entirely: confirmed live that CFL games were showing up with nowhere to actually navigate to them, because a dedup check meant to stop TheSportsDB's raw sport list from adding a redundant generic "American Football" menu entry was also (wrongly) applied to this addon's OWN curated category list - since NFL, CFB, and CFL are all classified as the same TheSportsDB sport ("American Football"), and NFL happens to be listed first, CFB and CFL were being silently skipped out of the menu every time, as if they didn't exist. Also fixed the actual cause of CFL games showing up mixed into the NFL listing itself (confirmed live: a real CFL game and a European League of Football game both appeared inside NFL) - the supplementary schedule source has no per-league split for American football, so it was merged in unfiltered for whichever of NFL/CFB/CFL happened to have a menu entry; now filtered by each game's real league name before merging, so NFL only shows NFL, CFL only shows CFL, etc. Both bugs together also explain why a real CFL game's own stream links weren't found when played from the (wrong) NFL section - the wrong sport was being passed to every stream resolver, none of which know to check CFL's actual listings when told to look for NFL. Fixed a narrow but real race condition behind the home screen occasionally failing to load a section on the first click (confirmed live, matched reports it "works on retry"): a background thread that pushes freshly-loaded data into the home screen can land mid-navigation and throw against an already-closing window; tightened from both sides so the window signals it's closing before doing anything else, and the background thread re-checks immediately before touching it. Also fixed the Sports section's page title showing a broken/unreadable placeholder character in the breadcrumb (e.g. "Videos / Starfleet / [?] Boxing") - a stadium/hockey emoji in the category title that this Kodi build's skin font can't render; replaced with plain text. Adult section: film titles are now cleaned of common scraping junk (duplicate year tags, resolution/release tags) before being displayed or used to check for a stream source - a mismatched messy title on one side of that check could cause a real, working film to be wrongly dropped as "no source"; the New Releases/Recently Added/Best Sellers listings were also found to skip the has-a-source check entirely (unlike every other Adult listing), so titles with no actual stream anywhere were shown and dead-ended on click - now filtered the same as everywhere else. Performer/actor search in the Adult section's unified search was a stub that always returned nothing ("no actor search API - skip for now") - built a real one backed by a cached full name index from the site's own per-letter actor pages. New sports stream source added (livetv902.me / livetv.sx family): covers a wide range of sports and leagues this addon didn't have a source for before; found via live investigation that its "alieztv"-type mirrors resolve through a plain, unobfuscated JS call to a real HLS URL - no WASM/P2P wall like embed.st - verified against a real live CFL game. Note: this source's availability was inconsistent in testing (worked reliably in some passes, not in others, without a clear cause) - it's wired in as a supplementary source alongside everything else, so it simply contributes nothing extra when it's not available rather than causing any problem. v2.3.219 - Fixed MLB Network and NHL Network (24/7 channels) not playing: verified live that daddylive.mov's signing CDN (fiveo4.casadenoval.uk) started rejecting every request with a bare 403, even a freshly-decoded, correctly-signed, not-yet-expired URL with the right Referer - this looked at first like the same un-fixable TLS-fingerprint wall documented elsewhere in this changelog for Cloudflare Turnstile, but confirmed by direct testing it isn't: the CDN now also requires the Sec-Fetch-Dest/Mode/Site "fetch metadata" headers a real browser always sends and that neither our scraper nor, importantly, Kodi's own player ever did - simply adding them (both to our own verification check and onto the URL Kodi's player actually opens, via the same header pipe-syntax already used elsewhere for Referer/User-Agent) resolves it. Also added a live-verification step this resolver was missing entirely: previously, once a mirror's obfuscated blob decoded into something that merely looked like a URL, that URL was handed straight to Kodi's player with no check that it would actually serve - now it's fetched and confirmed to return a real #EXTM3U playlist first, so a mirror that decodes but 403s (this exact bug) or serves an expired/dead link gets correctly skipped in favor of the next mirror instead of crashing playback. v2.3.218 - Fixed Adult section kicking the user all the way out of the addon on click, same class of bug as the Sports crash-out fixed in v2.3.216/217, but guaranteed to happen every time instead of intermittently: entering the Adult section shows a PIN entry prompt if one is set, and that prompt was popping up in the middle of the same window-activation sequence a Sports click goes through - any blocking dialog shown at that exact moment can make Kodi abandon the transition. The PIN check now happens before the home screen even starts navigating away, not during it. Also fixed a related bug found while fixing this: the "only ask for the PIN once per session" behavior never actually worked, because this addon runs with reuselanguageinvoker off (a fresh Python process per call, confirmed in addon.xml) - the old code stored the unlock flag in a plain in-memory variable that reset on every single click, silently re-prompting for the PIN every time despite the setting's own description promising otherwise. Now persisted properly so it actually only asks once. Also: the home screen's focus-highlight border around the selected poster is noticeably larger now - the previous release's ~2% bump turned out to be too subtle to see; also enlarged the matching per-row focus borders (there were two overlapping highlight mechanisms in the skin, only one of which was resized last time). v2.3.217 - Follow-up to v2.3.216's navigation fix, based on further live testing on the Firestick: the previous release stopped the "kicked all the way out of the addon" symptom, but a deeper live test showed the fix's own two-step handoff (jump to an empty placeholder screen first, then swap in the real category a moment later) could still get stuck - the second step silently failing to fire, leaving the user stranded on a permanently empty screen instead of the Sports (or Movies/TV/Live TV/Adult) page they clicked. Replaced that two-step handoff with a single direct jump straight to the clicked category, removing the fragile middle step entirely. Trade-off: Back out of a category may now return to Kodi's previous screen instead of this addon's home screen in some cases, rather than a category that may not load at all - confirmed working live against Sports. v2.3.216 - Fixed a real crash-on-navigate bug found by live-testing on the Firestick: clicking Sports (or any top-nav category) in the home screen could silently kick the user all the way out of the addon back to Kodi's own Add-ons screen, with no error dialog. Also: the dependency-check prompt (offers to install ResolveURL) was re-running on every single in-app navigation click, not just on first launch - could pop a blocking install prompt mid-navigation for no reason connected to what was actually clicked; now only runs when Home is genuinely (re)launching. Also: the home screen's focus-highlight border around the selected poster is now slightly larger (~2%) per user request, for better visibility. v2.3.215 - Fixed three real skin-navigation bugs found by live-testing on the Firestick with ADB: (1) an unprompted auto-relaunch, where backing all the way out to Kodi's own Add-ons screen would spontaneously reopen Starfleet's home a moment later with zero input - root cause was the addon's own root action relaunching Home on ANY visit to its plugin:// root with no fresh lock file present, including background metadata queries from Kodi/the active Kodi skin (e.g. Add-ons tile widgets), not just genuine user launches; now only relaunches when the Videos window is actually the one on screen. (2) The home screen's hero banner (title/plot/Play/More Info) could get stuck showing a previous section's item when switching to a section with no content yet (e.g. Live TV with no favorites saved) - it's now cleared instead of left stale. (3) Moving left/right at the very edge of a carousel row could unexpectedly jump focus to the top nav bar instead of stopping at the row - the row lists were missing their own left/right wrap targets, letting Kodi's automatic proximity navigation take over.\nv2.3.214 - Added a new working stream resolver: streame.center, a shared embed backend used by several front-end sites (e.g. powerstreams.site, realsportshd.buzz) that a raw embed link alone can't play (its ch##.php/hls.php pages need a decrypt.php exchange first, done automatically now) - verified live against a real MLB game. Rather than write one scraper per front-end site (most of them have no real schedule of their own to scrape - one 403s outright, another is just a static link directory), this runs as a universal post-processing step across every existing source (StreamsEast, CrackStreams, etc), so any sport those sources already cover gets this fix automatically the moment one of them happens to route through streame.center. Also fixed the repo's own landing page (index.html) linking to a stale repository.starfleet-1.0.11.zip instead of the current 1.0.13 - a fresh install via that page was pulling the old repository add-on even though addons.xml itself was already correct.\nv2.3.213 - Fixed CrackStreams returning 0 events for every sport, every time: its event-listing page was being fetched at /league/mlbstreams (etc.), which is a 404 - the site moved to /category/mlb/ (etc.) a while back, and even that correct page no longer has any scrapable per-game links in its static HTML (JS-rendered listing, like most of this ecosystem now). Rather than reverse-engineer another discovery API, this now builds the event page URL directly from the two team names in the title (CrackStreams' own URL pattern is the predictable /stream/<team>-vs-<team>, tried in both team orders) - verified live against a real game that this correctly finds the page and extracts its actual stream list, where before it always found nothing. Note: depending on the specific event, CrackStreams' own links may route through the same embed.st-family WASM-gated hosts documented as unfixable in previous releases - that's a limitation of whichever embed provider that event happens to use, not of this fix.\nv2.3.212 - New working stream source for MLB/NBA/NHL/NFL: mlb24all.ir and its sibling sites (nba24all.ir, nhl24all.ir, nfl24all.ir) were already listed in this addon's own code as a planned source, but the implementation was dead - it scraped for HTML anchor links that stopped existing once those sites became client-rendered apps, and it was never actually wired into the stream picker to begin with. Replaced it with a real implementation found via live network inspection: these sites run a clean, unauthenticated JSON API (GET .../api/v3/stateshot for the game/team catalogue, POST .../api/v2/generate_stream_info for a direct playable HLS link) - no login, no obfuscation, no WASM, just a straightforward API call. Verified live against an in-progress Blue Jays vs Rays game: returns real, independently-confirmed-working ESPN Home/Away broadcast links. This runs alongside every other source in the same merged link dialog, so a game covered by this source now shows up as extra "Link N" options next to StreamsEast/DaddyLive/etc.\nv2.3.211 - Fixed a real crash-on-play bug found by testing the Blue Jays game live on-device: the DaddyLive/TVNow24/7-channel resolver (used for the MLB/NHL Network channels and as the supplementary source merged into every sport event's link dialog) would, when none of a channel's mirrors could be decoded, hand back the raw unresolved mirror page URL on the theory that ResolveURL "might know it" â€” instead Kodi got a plain HTML page and crashed immediately with "error probing input format". Now returns nothing for that channel instead, so it's correctly dropped from the dialog rather than offered as a guaranteed-broken option. Also discovered and wired up a much more reliable resolution path for one whole class of these mirrors: some daddylive.mov mirrors point at tvnow247.top's own /embed/<channel> page, which used to fail outright (it's a client-rendered app with nothing scrapable in its HTML) â€” found via live network inspection that its player calls a clean JSON API (chat.cfbu247.sbs/api/resolve-dlstream) to get its real stream, so that's tried first now, with a live-playlist check before accepting it (a couple of channels' upstreams turned out to be genuinely offline right now, verified directly â€” not a scraper bug, just those specific feeds being down). StreamsEast (embed.st) links are confirmed to depend on a WASM+P2P ticket-exchange system with no static stream URL anywhere in the page - verified via live browser inspection that even a real browser only gets a playable stream after running embed.st's own obfuscated code, which can't be replicated from a Kodi Python addon - left as-is this release since that's a limitation of that specific host, not something scraping can fix.\nv2.3.210 - Fixed MLB (and every sport's) StreamsEast source: streamseast.is is dead (the domain no longer resolves at all); the site moved to streameasti.is with a different URL structure (no numeric event id, irregular section-name pluralization) and a different embed mechanism (source buttons carry a base64-encoded URL in a data-s attribute, swapped into the player by a JS click handler â€” the iframe's own src is always blank in the raw HTML, so the old scraper found nothing). Updated the domain, URL patterns, and added the data-s extraction, so StreamsEast now contributes real "Link N" options again for every sport, not just MLB. Verified against a real live Blue Jays game: get_event_streams now returns 3 StreamsEast links + 3 more from the TVNow247/DaddyLive source added in v2.3.209, all 6 shown together in one sequentially-numbered dialog (this merging was already automatic â€” fixing the two sources was the actual work). v2.3.209 - New: MLB Network 24/7 channel added to the MLB section â€” selecting it shows a Link 1/2/3 picker across three known-good daddylive.mov mirrors. New: full Live TV source added â€” TVNow247 (500+ channels scraped from tvnow247.top, adult channels excluded). New: live sports events scraped from tvnow247.top/schedule.json are now merged into each sport's event listing and used as a supplementary stream source everywhere, categorized by sport automatically. Fixed a real bug found while building these: the daddylive.mov channel resolver assumed every mirror-list JSON entry has the same {name,url} shape, but some pages use {name,id,url} with an extra field in between â€” entries in that shape were silently never matching. Also fixed: numeric-only channel ids (this addon's own MLB "399" test case, plus most of TVNow247's catalogue) were falling back to parsing the page's title tag for the real channel name, but title formats vary wildly ("Free X Live...", "Watch X Online...", "X Live Stream Free...") and that guess was unreliable â€” callers that already know the real name (the new TV channel list, the new events scraper) now pass it through explicitly instead of guessing, which took random-sample channel resolution from 0% to 100% in testing. v2.3.208 - v2.3.207 verified live: NHL Network now resolves and plays (confirmed reaching video decode), and Back from Movies/TV Shows/etc now correctly returns to the home screen. This release fixes the one remaining piece: the carousel focus highlight still wasn't showing, because the id=90 overlay control had a hardcoded <visible>false</visible> in the skin XML â€” Kodi re-evaluates XML visible conditions continuously, which silently overrides/no-ops any Python setVisible(True) call. Removed the XML condition; visibility is now owned entirely by home.py (explicitly hidden on init, shown/positioned on focus). v2.3.207 - NHL Network 24/7 channel still didn't play after v2.3.205's onhockey.tv fix, because onhockey.tv's own proxy for that channel (daddylive.php) is dead (404). Now resolves directly via daddylive.mov's channel mirror list, decoding the obfuscated embed script one mirror tier uses to get a fresh signed .m3u8. Also: fixed Adult section movie posters occasionally showing a neighboring film's cover art (nearest-match bug in the cover-art scraper). Also: home screen carousel focus highlight (the orange selection border on Movies/TV/etc rows) now actually renders â€” it was never appearing on some devices/Kodi builds even though selection itself worked. Also: Back from a section (Movies/TV Shows/etc) now correctly returns to the home screen instead of exiting past the addon into Kodi's own Videos section. v2.3.206 - Fix free/non-debrid streams not resolving: script.module.resolveurl was marked optional and pinned to a stale version (5.1.28) that was never actually hosted anywhere, so it was silently never installed. Now required, bumped to the real published 5.1.206, and pulled from the repository's new smrzips repo dir. v2.3.205 - Fix NHL Network (Sports section) not playing: onhockey.tv's live-channel page (used for the 24/7 NHL Network stream) embeds its player via JS config (src/file/source: "...m3u8") or a same-domain proxy iframe, not the plain stream links the scraper was looking for. Added JS-embedded m3u8 detection and a same-domain iframe follow-through, matching the extraction already used successfully for this exact channel in the Live TV section.

extension.description: Beautiful Soup is a Python library for pulling data out of HTML and XML files.

Elementum is a torrent finding and streaming engine. It doesn't go on torrent websites for legal reasons. However, it calls specially crafted add-ons (called providers) that are installed separately. This project is a fork of the well known, but no longer maintained Pulsar/Quasar projects from steeve and scakemyer. NOTE: install plugin.video.elementum-0.1.114.zip from the repository first, then manually install the matching plugin.video.elementum-0.1.114.<platform>.zip on top for your device's platform (e.g. windows_x64, android_arm64, linux_x64) and restart Kodi - binaries are split into per-platform zips to stay under GitHub's 100MB file size limit.
